turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay, quick one before lunch.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The Riverbend ferry timetable changes on the first of the month.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Which sailings move?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The early sailing moves from seven to half past six.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That breaks the school run for the Saltmarsh families.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Can we keep a seven o'clock sailing on weekdays?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Only if we drop the late Friday one.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Nobody uses the late Friday sailing anyway.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Right.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So we keep seven on weekdays and drop late Friday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Agreed, I'll tell the harbour office.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Do we need council sign-off for that?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No, timetable changes under an hour don't need it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. Harborlight kiln budget next.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: The kiln quote came in at forty two thousand.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's eight over what we planned.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Could we reuse the old kiln shelving to save some of it?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Maybe three thousand, not more.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Is the extra money coming from the ferry savings?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Partly, the dropped Friday sailing saves about two thousand a month.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Then we can cover the gap in four months.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Fine, I'll ask finance to split the payment.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Who checks the shelving is safe to reuse?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: I will, by Thursday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Great, that's everything.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thanks all.
